 Judgment

Disputing the validity and the legality of the order that is rendered by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bidar in MVC No.426/2017 dated 01.04.2019 the present appeal is preferred by the appellant/Insurance Company.

2. Heard Sri. Sharanabasappa M. Patil, the learned counsel for the appellant and Sri. Basavaraj R.
Math, the learned counsel for respondent No.6.

Despite service of notice, none appears for respondent Nos.1 to 5.
3.
The present is the appeal preferred by the Insurance Company disputing its liability to pay compensation to the claimants i.e. respondent Nos.1 to 5 herein.
The Tribunal through the impugned order, awarded a sum of Rs.15,21,200/- as compensation and directed the appellant herein to satisfy the same.

4. Making his submission with regard to the merits of the matter, the learned counsel for the appellant contends that the deceased-Hussain Ali [hereinafter referred to as NC:
2024:KHC-K:545-DB 'the deceased' for brevity] while traveling in an auto sustained injuries as the said auto turned turtle and he succumbed to the injuries.
The learned counsel submits that permit was issued for the auto to ply within the limits of Manna-E-Khelli village.
However, the auto was found proceeding beyond and exceeding the said limits.
The accident occurred when the auto was proceeding from Mailar (Khanapur) through Sangolgi-Bawagi road towards Aurad village, which is at a distance of 13 kms to Manna-E- Khelli town.
Learned counsel further states that as the permit condition was violated, the Insurance Company is not liable to pay any compensation.
He states that though said specific stand was taken and was established before the Tribunal, the Tribunal fastened the liability against the appellant-Insurance Company.
Hence, the present appeal is preferred.

5. To substantiate his version that no liability can be fastened against the insurer when the condition of permit is violated, learned counsel relied upon the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Rani & Ors. vs National NC: 2024:KHC-K:545-DB Insurance Company Ltd., & Ors.1.

entities.text: Rani & Ors. vs National NC: 2024:KHC-K:545-DB Insurance Company Ltd., & Ors.1.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: A perusal of the said decision goes to show that appreciating the contentions that the offending vehicle did not posses a valid permit to operate in the State of Karnataka and where the permit was limited to State of Maharashtra and where the offending vehicle had indeed crossed the State limits, the Court ordered to pay and recover.
Even in that case the Court did not exonerate the Insurance Company from total liability.

6. In the case on hand, as rightly submitted by the learned counsel appearing for respondent No.6,
the offending auto had just crossed the border of the village within which limits it was entitled to ply The Branch Manager vs Rizwana Begum And Ors on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105711019/
3 and was proceeding within the limits of the abutting village.

entities.text: Branch Manager vs Rizwana Begum And Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, as rightly contended by the learned counsel, the facts are rightly distinguishable.
It is not the case of the appellant that the offending vehicle did not posses a permit at all.
Stating that in the similar circumstances, the Insurance Company was ordered to satisfy the award, the learned counsel for respondent No.6 relied upon two decisions of this Court.
The Civil Appeal No. 9079 of 2017 decided on 31.07.2018 NC: 2024:KHC-K:545-DB first decision is the one which is rendered in MFA No.30752/2011 and batch matters dated 11.07.2018.

Dealing with the similar circumstances, this Court at para- 10 of the judgment observed as under:
"10.

There is no dispute about the autorickshaw having insurance coverage as on the date of accident; according to the insurance company, since six passengers travelled in it and that the accident occurred at a place beyond the area permitted for plying and therefore its liability to indemnify the owner gets exonerated.
It is not possible to accept this argument.
It is not the case that there was no permit at all for the autorickshaw.
It had a valid permit, but it was taken beyond the permitted limit.
There is some difference between the two.

If there is no permit at all, or if a transport vehicle is used for a purpose not allowed by the permit as envisaged in S.149(2)(a)(i)(c), the insurance company need not indemnify the liability of the insured for violation of policy condition.

But where a vehicle is taken beyond the limits, it cannot be said that there is violation of policy condition, it is contravention of permit condition which is punishable according to S.192A of the Motor Vehicles Act."
The second decision is the one which is rendered by this Court in MFA No.201648/2015 and batch matters dated NC: 2024:KHC-K:545-DB 26.09.2020.

In this matter referring the aforementioned decision, this Court at para-8 held as follows:
"8.

In view of the above, the contention of the learned counsel for the insurance company that since the offending vehicle did not have any permit to ply in the State of Andhra Pradesh, insurance company has no liability to satisfy the award amount cannot be accepted and accordingly the contention put forth in this behalf is rejected."

7. The material available on record makes it clear that the deceased boarded the offending auto on 26.03.2017 as a passenger and the driver of the said auto drove the same at a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and applied sudden break, due to which auto turned turtle and the deceased received injuries and ultimately succumbed to the injuries.
There is no denial of the fact that, there is no much distance between the permissible limits as per the permit and the place of accident.
8. Taking into consideration all these aspects, the Tribunal has rightly passed an award fastening the liability against the Insurance Company.

sentences.text: In the light of the discussion, that went on supra with regard to the merits of the matter, this Court does not find any grounds so as to interfere with the impugned order.
Though another contention with regard to the quantum awarded is raised, the appellant fails even on that count.

The Tribunal taking into consideration the dependency of the claimants over the income of the deceased who are none other than wife, children and mother of the deceased had awarded a just sum as compensation.
Therefore, the ultimate conclusion of this Court is that the appeal deserves to be dismissed.
10. Resultantly, the appeal stands dismissed without costs.
